_comment: AGENT: always read this file via the task-index-manager skill before reading or writing any task state. System tracker for ai-worldbuilder (ADR 002). Never add tasks for individual worlds here

tasks.title: logout_gate: work without fcntl (Windows)
tasks.notes: lib/blocks/logout_gate.py session_lock_held uses fcntl.lockf (POSIX only), so the logout gate and scripts/check_instance.py fail on Windows. Replace with a portable check (msvcrt.locking on Windows, or try opening the lock file exclusively). Keep the rule that session.lock existence proves nothing. Add a test with a fake lock.

tasks.title: Portability pass for Linux and Windows users
tasks.notes: Audit tool-repo assumptions before sharing the code: python3 vs py -3 in AGENTS.md and skills; jq/grep/zsh in hooks; pyproj OSTN15 lookup only checks Homebrew paths (lib/geo/world_frame.py); GDAL/ogr2ogr requirement for osm_extract; agent-soundboard cue must be optional; any absolute /Users paths left in tool docs. Document Windows as WSL-first unless fixed. Setup doc: docs/minecraft-instance-setup.md.

tasks.title: Give sealed bake-off answers a home outside worlds/
tasks.notes: Southampton Refine/instance/bakeoff-sealed/truth.json holds sealed bake-off answers that must stay out of agent view, and it sits in the donor instance being retired. Decide a location (outside worlds/ and the Minecraft instance), point bakeoff/model_bakeoff.py at it, document it in bakeoff/OVERVIEW.md. Blocks task 178.

tasks.title: Retire the donor Minecraft instances and old launcher profiles
tasks.notes: Owner's machine only, after a few days of use from ~/Projects/minecraft-mcp: delete Southampton Refine/instance and Minecraft Magic/instance (the Refine one still holds the scratch save 'New World', backed up in ~/Projects/minecraft-save-backups/2026-10-28/, and bakeoff-sealed/truth.json); remove launcher profiles 'southampton-refine' and 'fabric-loader-26.2'; update Minecraft Magic/README.md to name the new instance. Plan: docs/plans/shared-minecraft-instance.md.

tasks.title: Rename cell.origin to the home cell; drop stale top_of_world
tasks.notes: The new-world guide calls the start cell the home cell but the key is still cell.origin (lib/geo/cellmath.py origin_cell(), world_frame.py info, both world-frame.json files, unit_test_world, docs). Rename to cell.home with a clear error for the old key. Also remove top_of_world (254, stale: build range is Y -64..319, nothing reads it) from the frames and legacy_offsets_dict, and use 'origin' only for MC (0,0).

tasks.title: Test large block coordinates in the game for new-world 0/0 offsets
tasks.notes: New-world guide recommends offsets 0,0 so x = easting, z = -northing (about 442000, -115000 for Southampton). Unverified: client rendering, physics and region/cell tooling at coordinates in the hundreds of thousands. Build a throwaway world at such coordinates, check rendering jitter, entity movement, region file naming and cell ids, then confirm or tighten the guide (fallback: offsets = home rounded to 10 km).

tasks.title: osm_extract: resolve the vector_map provider from the world config
tasks.notes: shims/osm_extract.py hardcodes _PACKAGE = providers/geofabrik-hampshire (line 25), so a world with a different regional extract (Ventnor needed geofabrik-isle-of-wight) cannot use the shim and the Ventnor build ran a throwaway script instead. Resolve the vector_map provider id from the active world's config/local-providers.json (cell_sources.provider_package_dir) and fail clearly when none is set. Found in the Ventnor new-world run.

tasks.title: New worlds: generate or share osmconf.ini for the vector_map extractor
tasks.notes: The extract step needs an osmconf.ini; nothing in the tool repo creates it (no reference to it outside worlds), so the Ventnor run copied one by hand from Southampton. Either generate it when scaffolding a new world / provider, or point the extractor at one shared copy in the tool repo. Pair with the osm_extract provider-resolution task.

tasks.title: Scaffold command for a new world's vector_map provider
tasks.notes: In the Ventnor run the agent made geofabrik-isle-of-wight by hand-copying the Southampton extractor because the Hampshire extract does not cover the Isle of Wight. Add a command (or skill-driven script) that scaffolds a regional-extract provider for a new world from a Geofabrik extract name, including the osmconf.ini and the catalogue row, and checks the extract covers the bbox. Update the new-world-build skill section 3 to use it.

tasks.title: templates: .gitignore for a new world repo
tasks.notes: A new world is its own git repo but there is no template .gitignore for downloads/ and caches; the Ventnor run copied Southampton's by hand. Add one under templates/ (e.g. templates/new-world-site or a new templates/new-world-repo) and have the new-world-build skill copy it. The skill's close checklist currently says to copy an existing world's.

tasks.title: lidar_extremes: suggested y_offset can push tops over 319
tasks.notes: providers/ukdefra-lidar/review/lidar_extremes.py reports suggested_y_offset_for_ground_near_64, which only aims the DTM minimum near 64. For Ventnor (DTM 0-243 m, DSM 275 m) it suggested an offset that would put tops at 339, above the 319 build limit; the agent had to override it. Make the suggestion respect both limits (ground min >= -64 with margin, DSM max <= 319), or say plainly when no offset fits.

tasks.title: Shims fail from a plain checkout: import script_env needs PYTHONPATH=scripts:lib
tasks.notes: From a clean checkout with no .venv, python3 shims/lidar_extremes.py fails with ModuleNotFoundError: script_env (shims/lidar_extremes.py puts only the repo root on sys.path); it works with PYTHONPATH=scripts:lib. Same pattern for the other shims. Make shims add scripts/ and lib/ to sys.path themselves (or via _provider_shim), so the documented command works, then drop the PYTHONPATH prefix from the new-world-build skill.

tasks.title: Measure the first lidar fetch and record it in rules/slow-commands.md
tasks.notes: The fetch now prints [i/N] progress and per-tile and total elapsed time (task/lidar-fetch-progress). Run it on a real new world (e.g. Ventnor tile 455000E-75000N, DTM and DSM) and add the measured time and tile size to rules/slow-commands.md, then put the figure in the new-world-build skill's slow-fetch warning.
